distractorRationales.opt_c: Misconception: Requires multiple cycles across dozens or hundreds of epochs.
distractorRationales.opt_d: Misconception: Only learning rate is reset, not model weights.

questions.explanation: Cosine annealing decays η along a cosine curve for convergence, then resets η to a peak. This warm restart provides kinetic energy to jump out of sharp local minima into broad, flat basins.

questions.text: In matrix calculus for neural networks, given affine transformation y = W x + b where x in R^n, W in R^{m x n}, and scalar loss L, what are the exact gradients dL/dW and dL/dx in terms of incoming gradient delta = dL/dy in R^m?

options.text: dL/dW = delta * x^T  (outer product, shape m x n)  and  dL/dx = W^T * delta  (shape n x 1)
dL/dW = W * delta^T  and  dL/dx = delta * W
dL/dW = delta * W  and  dL/dx = x * delta^T
dL/dW = x * delta^T  and  dL/dx = W * delta

distractorRationales.opt_a: Correct: By multivariable chain rule: dL/dW_ij = (dL/dy_i) * (dy_i/dW_ij) = delta_i * x_j, so dL/dW = delta x^T. For input: dL/dx_j = sum delta_i W_ij, so dL/dx = W^T delta.
distractorRationales.opt_b: Misconception: Shape mismatch (W is m x n, delta^T is 1 x m).
distractorRationales.opt_c: Misconception: Dimensions are incompatible for matrix multiplication.
distractorRationales.opt_d: Misconception: Inverts outer product order and misses transpose on W.

questions.explanation: By vector-matrix chain rule, ∂L/∂W = δ xᵀ (yielding an m × n outer product) and ∂L/∂x = Wᵀ δ (propagating the gradient backward to the previous layer).
